evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'It fails in CI. Now it fails on your laptop too.' plus bold lede 'Rerun is a free command-line tool for backend engineers. It records a failing test run in CI and replays it on your machine' names what, who and how; the install box beside it ('$ npm install -g @rerun/cli', 'Copy install command') is the next step. As the engineer with a terminal open I could repeat it after one read.
evidence.fit: Brief facts all reflected: free/MIT/no account in the install note, 'A hosted team version is planned, not built' as an H2 with 'no date to announce', 'There are GitHub stars and no customer logos, so the proof on this page is the replay above and the source'. Show-don't-tell answered by the operable tape directly under the hero. A 'What a replay cannot do yet' section speaks to a distrustful engineer. Docked one point: the founder would have to verify invented product specifics (Node-only, child processes not recorded, 'It costs nothing when the run passes').
evidence.distinctiveness: The twin-track tape (CI-recorded column vs laptop column, with a 'rerun replay ci-8841' / 'npm test (no rerun)' toggle) comes straight from the product's job. The rest is a familiar dev-tool sequence: hero + install card, 2x2 mechanism grid, steps + code block, limits list, $0 pricing card, CTA band.
evidence.proof: 1440: tape controls and first three event rows are visible at y=546-900 in the first viewport. Toggling to 'npm test (no rerun)' turned 6 of 7 rows to 'differs' and the badge to 'PASS · not reproduced'; back to rerun gives 'FAIL · reproduced, 7 of 7 matched'. This answers my real doubt (does it actually make the flaky failure happen locally?). Numbers are consistent across the page: 7 events, the code block's 'pinned clock, 2 responses, 1 random draw, 14 env vars' matches the tape rows. Labelled 'Sample recording written for this page'. At 390 the tape starts below the first screen (panel top 919).
evidence.craft: Clean type scale and rules, consistent 44px buttons, no overflow at 1440/768/390/320 (probe and my check: overflow 0). Minor: at 768 the tape switches to the stacked phone layout and grows to ~1420px tall; inline text links (Read the docs, footer links) are 17-20px tall.
evidence.mobile: 390: H1 at 97-209, install card with full-width 44px 'Copy install command' at 558-602, Menu button opens a details dropdown and closing-on-link works (tapped 'Limits', menu closed, #limits at top 72). Tape is recomposed (outcome badge moved above the controls, rows labelled 'CI run'/'Laptop'), so feedback lands next to the buttons. But the panel is ~1860px tall at 390 and the 'Sample recording' label sits at its bottom (y~2794), far from where the demo starts.
evidence.honesty: Tape foot: 'Sample recording written for this page. It runs in your browser; nothing is installed, fetched or sent.' Code block: 'Example. Exact flags are in the docs.' and 'Command names and output are illustrative'. Primary action is a copy button that does exactly that ('Copied: npm install -g @rerun/cli'). Pricing and no-customers handled plainly. Minor: 'It costs nothing when the run passes' is an unsupported overhead claim, and at 390 the sample label is ~1900px below the start of the demo.
evidence.interaction: All three widths, operated: 'Copy install command' wrote 'npm install -g @rerun/cli' to the clipboard and showed 'Copied: ...' inline; 'Replay the run' animated rows with badge RUNNING and button 'Stop'; pressing Stop gave 'STOPPED AT 1/7'; full run ended 'FAIL · reproduced'; mode toggle switched to PASS; slider to 0 gave 'READY · Recording loaded'; ArrowRight on focused slider moved it to 2/7. No console errors. Small gaps: Escape does not close the phone menu (details stays open), and the tape loads already at 7/7 so the first visible state is the end.
evidence.copy: Written in the engineer's world: 'The test is not random. Its inputs are.', 'A setTimeout(1200) that crossed midnight in CI crosses midnight again on your laptop at two in the afternoon', 'Read this before you spend an afternoon on it.' Buttons say what happens ('Copy install command', 'Replay the run', 'View the source on GitHub'). No buzzwords found.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, the install action, and the tape's controls plus three recorded events (Date.now 23:59:58.912Z, Math.random) are in view, so the promise is backed. 390: promise, lede and Copy install command are in view, but no artifact; the tape heading starts at the very bottom edge.

problems: At 390 the demo is below the first screen and the panel is ~1860px tall, with the 'Sample recording written for this page' label at its far bottom rather than next to the data.

evidence.clarity: H1 'The test that only fails in CI, failing on your laptop.' is a slightly awkward fragment but understandable; lede 'Rerun records a failing test run in CI and replays it exactly where you can put a breakpoint in it... Free, MIT-licensed, one command to install' gives what and next step. Audience (backend engineers) is only implied, never named.
evidence.fit: Tone suits developers and the no-logos tension gets a deliberate 'Where the project stands' section ('You would normally find a row of company logos here...'), hosted version 'planned but not built; there is no waitlist'. But for a brief that says developers distrust marketing, the page invents measurements and project facts (2-4% overhead 'in our measurements', 'Two people, part time', reply SLAs, CI/runner support matrix, secret redaction), which a founder could not put live without rewriting.
evidence.distinctiveness: Serif editorial type with a mono wordmark and a dark asciinema-style terminal is a recognisable dev-tool look; the terminal replay itself is product-shaped, but a scripted terminal cast is a common pattern in this category and the rest is two-column text sections and an FAQ accordion.
evidence.proof: Terminal autoplays in the first screen at 1440 (top 619) and shows a replay ending '2 passing · 1 failing · identical to CI run 4821' and 'rerun diff ... 0 differ'. But it is a fixed playback the visitor cannot vary (no with/without comparison), it is presented as 'a recording of a real replay session' rather than a labelled example, and the copy contradicts the widget: the note says the red tick is where the test fails '2,003 ms in', while the tick and the failing line sit at 0:05.6 on the 0:08.8 bar (FAIL_AT 5620 ms). At 390 the result lines are cut off.
evidence.craft: Good serif typography and measure at 1440. Defects: player controls are 25px tall (Replay/Pause and '1×' buttons, scrub 28px); hero at 1440 leaves the right half of the first screen empty above the terminal; at 390 the terminal content is clipped at the right edge (scrollWidth 560 vs clientWidth 358).
evidence.mobile: 390: no page-level overflow and the terminal begins in the first screen (top 537), nav fits inline. But inside the terminal 8 lines are cut at the right edge, including '✗ refunds within the return window (2,003...', '...identical to CI ru' and '0 diffe', readable only by scrolling the terminal sideways. Play and speed buttons are 25px tall; footer links 17px.
evidence.honesty: Replay note: 'This is a recording of a real replay session, played back in the page' for a session the brief does not supply. FAQ: 'roughly 2–4% on the test run itself, in our measurements on Jest suites between 500 and 5,000 tests. Numbers and the benchmark script are in the repository.' Status: 'Two people, part time. Issues get a reply within a few days; pull requests get a review within a week.' 'A typical recording ... is 1–5 MB.' 'The repository also includes the recording from the session above, examples/ci-8f3a2c'. None of these are in the brief and all are stated as fact. The copy button itself is honest.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: autoplay ran to 0:08.8 and the button became 'Replay' with label 'done'; Play/Pause toggled (paused at 0:01.6, label 'paused'); speed cycled 1×→2×→4×→1×; scrubbing to 5700 showed 12 lines, to 0 showed 2; End key on the focused slider jumped to 0:08.8; Copy turned to 'Copied' and reverted after 1.6s, clipboard held the command; all 6 FAQ items opened. No console errors. Control targets are small (25px) and there is nothing to choose, only to watch.
evidence.copy: Mostly specific and plain ('Three commands, start to breakpoint', 'Why not just retry the test?'), FAQ answers the questions an engineer actually asks. Docked for the awkward H1 fragment, the '2,003 ms in' vs 5.6 s contradiction, and unsupported generalisations ('which is where most "only in CI" failures come from').
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, install command with Copy, and the terminal starting its replay are in view; the failing line arrives near the bottom edge after ~5s and the controls and the note are below the fold. 390: promise, Copy and the top of the terminal are visible, but its lines are already clipped at the right.

problems: Fabricated proof stated as fact: '2–4% ... in our measurements on Jest suites between 500 and 5,000 tests', 'This is a recording of a real replay session', maintainer count and response-time commitments, a bundled examples/ci-8f3a2c recording.
At 390 the terminal artifact's key result lines ('identical to CI run 4821', '0 differ', the failing test line) are cut off and need sideways scrolling inside the terminal.
The demo is watch-only and its own caption contradicts it ('fails 2,003 ms in' vs the tick at 0:05.6); player buttons are 25px tall.

reason: As the engineer, A's tape lets me flip between 'rerun replay' and plain 'npm test' and watch the midnight-coupon failure reproduce or vanish, which answers whether it works, and every sample is labelled. As the founder, I could ship A after checking a few product specifics; B asserts benchmarks, maintainer SLAs and a 'real' session I never supplied, and its terminal clips its own conclusion on a phone. I would change my mind only if B's numbers and facts were real and its terminal wrapped at 390.
